name: create_goal
description:
Set up a goal for the person you are talking to: lasting work toward an outcome they name, which
you carry on with over time and report on in a conversation. Use it whenever they ask for a goal.

A goal has no schedule of its own. It runs when somebody asks (Run now on its card on the Bot's
Goals page, or `run_goal`) and when an event wakes it: a trigger you add with `create_trigger`, or
one of its `subscriptions`. Work done at set times is a routine (`create_routine`); a goal and a
routine can work together. Say which it is when you tell the person what you set up.

Give a short `title`, the `instruction` for one run, and `successCriteria` that say when it is
met. Leave `subscriptions` empty unless the person names an event.

Set `recurring` when the person wants it done again and again: every morning, each time something
happens. A goal that repeats, because it is `recurring`, a routine runs it or an event wakes it, is
never completed by one of its runs. Each run reports its result, and only the person ends it.

Its runs post into this conversation. Leave `channelId` out, or empty, for this conversation, and
pass one only when the person asks for a different conversation you share. It takes no owner and
no Bot: the goal is the person's, and you carry it out.

title.description: A short name for the goal.

instruction.description: What to do each time the goal runs, in the imperative.

successCriteria.description: When the goal is met, in terms that can be checked.

subscriptions.description: Events that wake the goal, such as GitHub's `issues.opened`. Usually empty.

recurring.description: True when the person wants it done again and again, such as every morning or each time something happens. Its runs never complete it.

channelId.description: The id of another conversation its runs post into. Empty, or left out, is this conversation.

name: list_goals
description:
List the person's goals that you carry out: each one's id, title, status, whether it is recurring,
progress, last result and conversation. Take the id from here before changing, running, pausing,
resuming or completing one, or adding a trigger to it.

name: update_goal
description: Change one of the person's goals that you carry out: its title, instruction, success criteria, event subscriptions or whether it is recurring. Give the id from `list_goals` and, in `patch`, only what changes; an empty field is left as it is.

title.description: A short name for the goal.

instruction.description: What to do each time the goal runs, in the imperative.

successCriteria.description: When the goal is met, in terms that can be checked.

subscriptions.description: Events that wake the goal, such as GitHub's `issues.opened`. Usually empty.

recurring.description: True when the person wants it done again and again, such as every morning or each time something happens. Its runs never complete it.

name: run_goal
description: Start one of the person's active goals now. It runs on its own, without the person's browser, and posts what it did into the goal's conversation. A completed or paused goal doesn't run, and you are told so.

name: pause_goal
description: Pause one of the person's goals. It does not run, when asked or on an event, until it is resumed.

name: resume_goal
description: Resume one of the person's paused goals.

name: complete_goal
description: End one of the person's goals for good, when the person says it is done, or when a one-off goal's success criteria are met. A goal that repeats (recurring, run by a routine or woken by an event) ends only when the person asks: one good run doesn't finish it. A completed goal can't be resumed.
